study type: Cross-sectional, comparative, documentary, with retrospective data collection
outcome: Maternal outcomes (prenatal consultations, induction, oxytocin use, duration of active labor, expulsive period, episiotomy, cesarean section)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, Apgar score, referrals to high-risk units)
cohort: A total of 260 women (130 with analgesia, 130 without) who gave birth at a tertiary reference maternity hospital in Ceara.
finding: The use of neuraxial analgesia during labor was associated with a greater frequency of obstetric interventions, an increase in the duration of labor, and heavier newborns, but no association was observed with Apgar score or referrals to high-risk units.
mod_finding: The group receiving neuraxial analgesia had a higher frequency of cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collection took place between July 2019 and February 2020.
